description:
FILED s470bt (Opus, 2026-09-06) by the B6 IR conformance corpus (3 cases).
#1271 (completed) fixed the LEXICAL spelling: `open(my $fh, ...)` that FAILS
now leaves $fh defined, because perl creates the handle before it opens.  The
ELEMENT spellings were not covered.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL main cd34df72):

  my @a; my $ok  = open($a[0], "<", "/nonexistent")?1:0;
  printf "arr ok=%s defined=%s\n", $ok, (defined $a[0]?1:0);
  my %h; my $ok2 = open($h{k}, "<", "/nonexistent")?1:0;
  printf "hsh ok=%s defined=%s\n", $ok2, (defined $h{k}?1:0);

  perl   arr ok=0 defined=1 / hsh ok=0 defined=1
  PCL    arr ok=0 defined=0 / hsh ok=0 defined=0

And the value `close` returns on such a handle:

  my $fh; open($fh, "<", "/nonexistent"); my $r = close($fh);
  printf "close=[%s]\n", (defined $r ? $r : "undef");

  perl   close=[]       (a defined empty string -- the false perl returns)
  PCL    close=[undef]

CORPUS CASES: 299-sprintf 308-sprintf 309-sprintf.

=== DONE (s473f) ===
Both halves.  The ELEMENT half fell out of #1309's place fix: with a box in the
place, %p-autoviv-failed-handle (#1271) has something to vivify, so a failed
`open($a[3],...)` leaves a closed glob there and grows the array to four
elements, as perl does.  The CLOSE half is #1307's: perl's false from `close`
is a DEFINED EMPTY STRING.  Corpus rows 299-io / 308-io / 309-io left
ir-conform/known-fail.tsv.  Commits a3d13bce + 5a952fce.
subject: SILENT WRONG (residue of #1271, found by the ir-conform corpus): a FAILED `open` into an ARRAY or HASH ELEMENT does not autovivify the handle, and `close` on a failed handle returns undef where perl returns ''
